A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LiveOIBench research work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of LLMs on LiveOIBench, including contest scores, human comparisons, scaling experiments, and reasoning-trace analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark evaluations and appendix analyses and additionally reports statement-rephrasing and adversarial-perturbation results.

M1.justification: The benchmark-construction approach, offline judge, and code-generation procedure are retained. The added contamination experiments and maintenance documentation do not introduce a new proposed model or inference algorithm.

E1.justification: The underlying 403 problems, 72 contests, 14 Olympiads, and existing programming-language coverage remain unchanged. v3 extends evaluation to altered input conditions, including statements with examples removed and tokens masked, alongside semantic rephrasing.

E2.justification: Grok-4-Fast and Claude-Sonnet-4.5 newly participate in the algorithm-tag comparison in Table 3. Both already appeared in v2's full leaderboard, so their added Table 2 rows largely redisplay existing comparisons; the full leaderboard's comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 introduces original/rephrased comparisons on 71 problems and example-removal and 10%, 30%, and 50% token-masking conditions. Appendix A.1 changes the stated human-results total from 46 to 50, with three contest-availability flags revised. The retained leaderboard is unchanged, and recomputation is not established. Existing sampling and decoding settings remain the same.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 and Figure 4 add a substantive intervention-based contamination analysis across three model families: testing robustness to semantic rephrasing versus degradation when useful statement information is removed. This adds a new class of evidence beyond v2's temporal, familiarity, and code-similarity correlations. Existing language, scaling, prompt-sensitivity, and reasoning-quality analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 4 newly reports paired standardized effect sizes, d_z, for adversarial perturbations. Existing prompt-variant means and standard deviations, correlation statistics, and inter-model agreement estimates are retained. No increase in repeated runs or seeds is reported.

E6.justification: v3 adds perturbation outcomes and Grok/Claude algorithm-tag scores while retaining the full leaderboard and appendix tag-table values. Figure 4 reports GPT-OSS-120B original/rephrased relative scores of 33.40/33.36. The new Qwen3-14B row in Table 3 gives mathematics 64.29, conflicting with 61.54 in both versions' appendix tables without an explained setting change. Appendix E.6 also corrects the 268.33% improvement's category from string manipulation to segment tree.

T1.justification: The Elo equation, difficulty mappings, metric definitions, and mathematical content of the retained examples are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, derivation, or formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: The benchmark contributions, headline human-performance gap, and reasoning-allocation claims remain stable. The abstract modestly qualifies the update claim from planned 'contamination-free updates' to updates that 'reduce contamination risk'.

C2.justification: v3 explains how rephrasing and information-removal tests distinguish semantic understanding from statement recall. Section 5.3 also explicitly acknowledges that low solution similarity cannot rule out exposure to related algorithms, narrowing v2's stronger interpretation that models actively reason and generate novel solutions.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.5 documents maintenance operations, model/contest eligibility relative to cutoff dates, and leaderboard time filtering. Appendix A.1 newly describes fallback medal thresholds and additional test-case quality checks, while E.4 illustrates rephrasing. These are documentation additions; the PDFs do not establish changes to the underlying retained procedures.

R1.justification: v3 adds Riddell et al. (2024) and Dekoninck et al. (2024) to frame contamination and its detection. The broader benchmark positioning remains stable; numerous other reference edits update publication metadata or consolidate duplicate entries.

P1.justification: v3 edits the abstract and prose, reorders contamination and error-pattern subsections, expands the main-text language discussion, and relocates future-direction and prompt material. The six-section main narrative and most substantive passages remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column presentation with reformatted headers, tables, and captions. Scaling plots are merged into Figure 6, reasoning panels are split between the main text and appendix, and the error plot moves to the appendix. Figure 4 is new, and the main comparison displays are expanded.

improvement.justification: The new perturbation tests supplement v2's observational contamination checks, while more qualified interpretation and maintenance documentation improve evidential clarity. These gains are limited by incomplete rewriting/masking specifications and new main-versus-appendix discrepancies for Qwen3-14B. With the core benchmark and full leaderboard retained, the evidence supports a modest overall improvement.
